subject: Localized benchmarking + regression watchlist — next steps and pilot kickoff
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Lingua Solutions (model recommendations + shortlist)

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery with Lingua (Lina + Pieter on the call). High-level: they need a cross-locale assistant for EU (FR/DE/ES/IT) and APAC (JA/KO) customer-facing flows — emphasis on politeness/formality control, low hallucination for billing/legal Qs, and strict PII handling. Key constraints: many short-turn chats (avg 40–80 tokens), sometimes 2–3 successive clarifications; latency SLO must be <= 400ms p50 for web tier.

What I captured as immediate risks and model-fit items: 
- FR/DE: regressions on formal/legal register; hallucination sensitivity (especially for contract snippets).
- JA/KO: high sensitivity to honorifics and polite forms — we should evaluate per-register prompts.
- Throughput: they'd prefer dedicated pools later but want hosted pilot first.

Recommended short model shortlist for pilot (per locale classes):
- Lightweight autoreg (fast) for short-turn flows: Mistral-7B-instruct (int8) — candidate for FR/ES
- Mid-sized instruction-tuned: Llama-3-13B-FT (4-bit quantized) — balance accuracy/latency (DE/IT)
- High-quality fallback (heavy): Llama-3-70B-int8 / Llama-2-70B for rare compliance/legal prompts (APAC + formal DE/FR)

Attachments: lingua_benchmark_summary_20270725.csv (call-level microbenchmarks), prompt_pack_eu_apac_v1.json (initial prompt templates). I've uploaded the raw evaluation spreadsheet to the Drive link in metadata.

Asks / next steps: 
1) Neha — please draft a focused prompt-pack specifically for FR/DE formal register (include negative examples and few-shot patterns).
2) Marissa — can you map these model candidates to our recommended quantization/batching profiles (cost vs latency tradeoffs)?
3) Ben — prepare a minimal pilot config (1-week A/B, target languages FR/DE/JA) with clear metrics (see below).

Suggested pilot DoD (so we can commit to Lingua):
- Latency: p50 <= 400ms, p95 <= 900ms for web tier
- Quality: human MOS >= 4.0 for FR/DE, hallucination rate < 3% on the legal prompt set
- Safety: no PII leakage in 500 random convo samples

I'll loop Lina once we have the prompt-pack and pilot config. If we can aim to ship the pilot by Aug 2 (kickoff Aug 4) that keeps the commercial timeline intact.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal AE, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-07-25T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Lingua Solutions (model recommendations + shortlist)

Thanks Rishi — good notes. Quick clarifications and additions from the ML side: 
1) Regression watchlist (what to monitor during pilot):
   - Register drift: compare MOS on formal vs informal prompts; flag if formal MOS drops >0.3 vs baseline.
   - Hallucination spikes on legal Qs: track hallucination_rate per model and abort rollout if >5% sustained for 48 hours.
   - Tokenization mismatches for JA/KO: ensure we use the same tokenizer and verify prompt truncation behavior for 4-bit quantized paths.

2) Prompt-pack ask: I'll take lead on FR/DE formal register templates. I'll include 20 positive examples, 20 adversarial negative examples, and 10 edge-cases that mimic billing/legal paraphrases. I'll attach a first draft by EOD Jul 26 (see prompt_pack_eu_apac_v1.json attachment).

3) Pilot measurement harness: we should instrument automatic checks (exact-match where applicable, semantic-similarity scoring via embedding cosine, and a small human panel for MOS). I'll prepare an eval harness and a short README pointing to the Drive file.

Note on models: for DE formal legal we may need the heavy fallback more often than expected — recommend we configure automatic fallback to the larger model only for inputs that match a regex for contract/legal keywords. That will limit cost.

I also spotted a couple of odd results in the CSV: FR baseline MOS looks lower on a subset of polite-form prompts — likely prompt template mismatch. I'll highlight rows 42–48 in the sheet.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. ML Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Lingua Solutions (model recommendations + shortlist)

Putting in specifics for the pilot ops and model-config mapping. Summary below, will drop the pilot_config_v1.yaml to the thread attachments once Ben confirms infra capacity.

Model -> Profile mapping (initial):
- Mistral-7B-instruct (int8): low-cost fast-path, batch size 8, target p50 = 220–320ms on hosted GPU GVM-1 (good for FR/ES)
- Llama-3-13B-FT (4-bit): medium path, batch size 4, p50 = 420–520ms (DE/IT)
- Llama-3-70B-int8: fallback for legal/finalize flows, no batching (or batch=1), p50 ~= 900–1200ms — route only when the input matches the legal pattern or user requests expert-level answer

Cost control ideas:
- Autoscale with burst cap to keep cost predictable; enable prefix cache for common FAQ flows (Lingua has a high repeat rate).
- Short-circuit to deterministic templates for billing lookups (strip model call) where possible.

Pilot metrics (concrete):
- MOS (human): target >= 4.0 for FR/DE; track per-model and per-prompt-type
- Hallucination rate: computed by the eval harness; threshold for rollback = 5%
- Latency: p50/p95 per model and per region
- Cost: $/k tokens for pilot week vs baseline estimate — track daily burn

I'll draft the pilot_config_v1.yaml with two A/B arms (Mistral vs Llama-13B for FR; Llama-13B vs 70B-fallback for DE legal subset). Ben — can you confirm we have hosted slots available Aug 4–11? If not, we'll pivot to a later start.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Proposed kickoff: Aug 4 as you suggested. We'll hold a 30-minute kickoff to sync on metrics, data ingestion, and success criteria. Can you send two proposed time slots (Aug 4 morning US / Aug 4 afternoon CET)?

Looking forward to seeing the prompt-pack and pilot config.

Best,
